data.text:
Rt. Rev. Dr. Orazio Bettachini  -  A
Paternal Founder

Rt. Rev. Dr. Orazio Bettachini, an Italian belonging to the
congregation of the Oratorians was consecrated bishop in 1846 and two years
later he was made the Pro-Vicar of the Jaffna Vicariate. In 1849, he became the
first Vicar Apostolic of Jaffna and continued in that office until 1857 when he
died rather prematurely when only 47.

Arriving in Colombo in 1842 he went to Kandy in 1843. He felt the need of a Catholic school in
Kandy and founded one in 1844 which was the precursor for St. Antony’s
College. This school-founding experience
had given him confidence to found later on St. Patrick’s College as well as
number of other schools. He came to
Jaffna for the first time on 30 April 1846. Mgr. Bettachini’s first priority in
Jaffna was to establish schools with facilities for English education and
refurbishing the already existing Tamil schools. For his plans he was able to count on the
support of the Catholic laity in Jaffna. These industrious laity especially those belonging to the Cathedral
functioned as a powerful spur to achieve his vision especially through the
Jaffna Catholic School Society established by Mgr.Bettachini. The outcome of the tireless efforts made by
Mgr. Bettachini as well as the energetic Catholic laity of the Cathedral was
the Jaffna Catholic English Boys’ School in 1849.

In the early stages there was no permanent abode for this
institution. There was no Bishop’s House and Mgr.Bettachini was staying in the
presbytery of the Church of Our Lady of Refuge and the English School was
functioning in a temporary building in this Church premises. In August 1849 Mgr. Bettachini took up residence in the house
where the present Bishop’s House is. The
school was also shifted to the present Cathedral compound in 1850. An Irish
gentleman, Mr. Patrick Foy became the Headmaster and there were 50 students.

The Jaffna Catholic English Boys’ School was later christened
as St. Patrick’s College on 10th Jan. 1881.
